newsitem.title: CANADA: Syncrude Canada production declines in first half.
newsitem.headline: Syncrude Canada production declines in first half.

text.p: Syncrude Canada Ltd, Canada's biggest oil sands operation, said on Friday that its synthetic oil production slipped in the first half of 1997 because of a maintenace turnaround.
But output from the mining, extraction and upgrading operation was still on target to reach record levels for the full year, the company said.
Syncrude, a joint venture of several oil companies, said it pumped out an average of 181,200 barrels of synthetic oil a day during the period, down from 191,200 in the first half of 1996.
The shipments totalled 32.8 million barrels for the six-month period, down from 34.8 million last year.
"We are targeting to produce a record 76 million barrels in 1997, an average of 208,000 barrels per day," Syncrude Chairman and Chief Executive Eric Newell said in a statement.
"I am also pleased to report a return on capital employed of 13.2 percent on a 12-month rolling basis."
Total unit costs, including administrative, research and financing, for the first two quarters were C$17.03 a barrel, compared to C$15.51/barrel for the first half of 1996, the company said.

"This was due to lower production as a result of a significant increase in the scope, and timing, of maintenance turnaround activities in 1997, in order to enhance reliability and prepare the plant for higher levels of future production," Syncrude said.
By early June, all units returned to service and the plant has since operated efficiently at high production rates, Syncrude said, adding that total unit costs in June fell to C$11.48 a barrel.
Revenue for the first six months totalled C$942 million, up from C$932 million in the same period of 1996, as prices for its output more than offset lower production volumes, Syncrude said.
The price for Syncrude's synthetic oil averaged C$28.72 a barrel, compared to C $$2 .80 a barrel in the first half of 1996.
Syncrude, located north of Fort McMurray, Alberta, is the world's largest producer of synthetic crude oil.

Its partners include Imperial Oil Ltd, Petro-Canada, Gulf Canada Resources Ltd, Athabasca Oil Sands Investments Inc, Canadian Oil Sands Investments Inc, Alberta Energy Co Ltd, Canadian Occidental Petroleum Ltd, Mitsubishi Oil Co Ltd unit Mocal Energy Ltd and Murphy Oil Corp. ((Jeffrey Jones, Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
